name: Sulfur Crown Agriculture
full_legal_name: Sulfur Crown Agriculture & Terraforming Sovereign Corponation
employees: 540,000 direct field and processing workers; 80,000 administrative
sovereign_territory: The Crown Territories — a discontinuous patchwork of 23 agricultural and remediation zones across former Indiana, Ohio, and Michigan farmland totaling approximately 800,000 acres. Connected by Sulfur Crown's private rail network. Each zone operates under local Crown law.
founding_story: The collapse of industrial Midwestern farming in the 2030s left millions of acres of chemically exhausted, flood-damaged, and contamination-blighted land essentially worthless. Agro-chemist Beaumont Jarvis saw an opportunity no one else wanted. In 2136, he began purchasing blighted farmland at near-zero valuations and applying his proprietary sulfur-catalyzed bioremediation process — a brutal, fast-acting soil restoration technique that worked spectacularly but left the land chemically dependent on Crown's own fertilizer compounds. Critics called it 'agricultural addiction.' Jarvis called it 'a sustainable relationship.' By 2144, Crown controlled enough food-producing territory to meaningfully threaten the caloric supply of three million GLMZ citizens, at which point sovereignty was less a legal argument than a statement of existing fact.
security_force: The Fieldwarden Corps — 35,000 heavily armed agricultural security personnel deployed across Crown Territories. Fieldardens are notorious for aggressive anti-poaching enforcement (the 'poaching' of crops, soil samples, or Crown's proprietary fertilizer compounds). They operate armored agricultural vehicles modified for combat. Rural communities near Crown Territories regard them with a mixture of economic dependency and deep fear.
key_detail: Sulfur Crown's remediation process, while genuinely effective at restoring blighted soil, renders the restored land chemically dependent on Crown's proprietary AUREATE fertilizer compound. Stopping AUREATE application causes rapid soil collapse within two growing seasons. This has created a captive market of independent farmers and smaller corponations who sold or leased land to Crown, accepted remediation, and now cannot exit the relationship without destroying their agricultural base.
relationship_to_big_20: Sulfur Crown is a Big 20 member but occupies a peculiar position: they are simultaneously resented and indispensable. Ironclad Agrisystems competes with them directly and bitterly in contested agricultural zones. Ouroboros Energy and Crown have a territorial dispute over former industrial land in Ohio that has produced three armed standoffs in the past decade. Crown supplies food inputs to Lacuna Genomics for agricultural genomics research under a contract that both parties describe as mutually beneficial and observers describe as mutually coercive.
full_text: Sulfur Crown Agriculture & Terraforming Sovereign Corponation (SCAT-G) controls the Crown Territories, an 800,000-acre patchwork of remediated and active farmland spread across the former American industrial heartland of Indiana, Ohio, and Michigan. Founded in 2136 by agro-chemist Beaumont Jarvis on the insight that ecological catastrophe creates acquisition opportunity, Sulfur Crown has transformed some of the most chemically devastated land in the Great Lakes corridor into productive agricultural zones — at a price. Crown's sulfur-catalyzed bioremediation process works, but the soil it produces is chemically dependent on Crown's proprietary AUREATE fertilizer line, a dependency that functions as a permanent revenue stream and a permanent lever of control over anyone who accepted Crown's remediation services. With Φ670 billion in annual revenue, a Φ2.9 trillion valuation, and 620,000 employees operating across 23 sovereign zones connected by private rail, Sulfur Crown is one of the most physically extensive corponations in GLMZ. Their Fieldwarden Corps — 35,000 armed agricultural security personnel in combat-modified farm vehicles — enforces Crown law across territories where the nearest alternative authority may be hundreds of miles away. The nickname 'Yellow Death,' applied by rural communities in Crown Territory border zones, refers both to the sulfurous yellow tint of treated soil and to the economic fate of communities that become dependent on Crown's food supply chains. Beaumont Jarvis died in 2151. His daughter, Cressida Jarvis-Mole, now runs the corponation with a reportedly tighter fist.

glmzTerritory.description: The Crown Territories — discontinuous network of 23 agricultural and remediation zones across Zones 8-10. Former industrial brewing infrastructure converted to large-scale fermentation-based food production using the same equipment. Zone 8 sovereign territory is the most densely populated outside of Chicago, because industrial food production at scale requires human workers.
glmzTerritory.grayZoneRelationship: Employs Gray Zone labor from Zones 8-10 on short-term contracts that are technically renewable and practically permanent.
